clue.text: Getting straight to the point in a murder, perhaps

definitions.text: Getting straight to the point in a murder, perhaps

parts.words: Getting straight to the point in a murder, perhaps
parts.note: a murder is the collective noun for a group of crows, so going directly somewhere is pictured as how those birds travel

explanation.surface: A detective cuts to the chase in a murder case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murder' looks like a crime, but a murder of crows is the flock's collective name; the phrase means by the most direct route.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in a direct line, which is how one travels when heading straight for a destination.

clue.text: Tornado gutted ship's launch

indicators.note: a gutted thing has had its insides removed, so only the first and last letters of tornado remain

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the usual abbreviation before a ship's name

explanation.surface: A twister wrecks a vessel as it is being launched.
explanation.definitionFit: To toss something is to throw it, and launching an object into the air is a synonym for that.

clue.text: Block that is housing politician and journalist

indicators.note: housing means holding within, so the abbreviation for that is surrounds the other letters

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is
MP, Member of Parliament
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's standard journalist

explanation.surface: Someone asks which block of flats houses an MP and a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: To block someone's progress is to hinder or obstruct it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Colours in evening paper

definitions.meaning: colours are a regiment's flag, also called its banner
the Evening ... is London's evening newspaper, often called just the ...

explanation.surface: Something printed in colour in the evening newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimental flag is a banner carried in battle, and London's evening daily bears that same name.

clue.text: Information is somewhat twisted

indicators.note: twisted here means turned round, so the phrase for somewhat is read backwards

parts.note: somewhat means a tad, a little

explanation.surface: A claim that some information has been slightly distorted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' looks like a modifier of twisted, but it gives A TAD, which 'twisted' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts and figures collected for reference or analysis are synonymous with information.

clue.text: Main actor upset performing Much Ado about Nothing

indicators.note: performing suggests putting on a show, so the words main actor upset are acted out in a new order

explanation.surface: The leading man throws a tantrum while staging Shakespeare's comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Much Ado about Nothing' looks like the play being performed, but it is the definition, read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a great fuss over something trivial, exactly what the play's title says in plain words.

clue.text: Vagrants turned on mother, daughter and son

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the word on is reversed

parts.note: MA is an informal word for mother
D, the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
S, the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Homeless people round on a family of mother, daughter and son.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanderers with no settled home are vagrants, and nomadic peoples roam similarly.

clue.text: Mauritian is confused about literature and philosophy

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around the abbreviation for literature
confused means mixed up, so the letters of Mauritian is are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man from Mauritius is bewildered by books and philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bentham and Mill's doctrine of the greatest good for the greatest number is a school of ethics.

clue.text: Pure Charlie and speed

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
haste means speed

explanation.surface: Someone praises a man named Charlie as pure and fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtuous and free from sexual impurity, an adjective synonym of pure.

clue.text: Fellow challenging no good official

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: no here means without, so the abbreviation for good is dropped

parts.note: daring means challenging, as in a daring climb

explanation.surface: A man defies a corrupt public servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior bureaucrat in imperial China, and by extension any high-ranking public official.

clue.text: General put in doctored cards to make cut

indicators.note: put in means inserted, so the general's abbreviation goes inside the shuffled letters
doctored means tampered with, so the letters of cards are altered

explanation.surface: A general cheats with a marked deck to cut the cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of meat: the bony neck of mutton is the scrag end, a cheap stewing joint in British butchery.

clue.text: Peeled mottled fruit

indicators.note: peeled means with the skin taken off, so the outer letters are removed

parts.note: dappled means mottled, spotted

explanation.surface: Fruit with blotchy skin has been peeled.
explanation.definitionFit: A common orchard fruit, a specific example of the general term.

clue.text: Part of world sailor captured in song

indicators.note: captured in means held inside, so the sailor goes within the word for song

parts.note: an aria is a song in opera
AB, able-bodied seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor's travels to some region are celebrated in song.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula of south-west Asia is a region of the globe.

clue.text: Heavyweight boxer's first international defence

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was the famous heavyweight boxing champion

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word boxer's is taken

explanation.surface: A heavyweight fighter's first international title defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim of being elsewhere when a crime occurred is a legal defence.

clue.text: Harp on about Annie, say

indicators.note: about here means around in any order, so the letters of harp on are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going on and on about a girl called Annie.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Orphan Annie is the comic-strip and musical heroine; 'say' marks her as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie of the musical is a parentless child, an example of the category.

clue.text: Queen's adviser possibly supporting dodgy deal

definitions.note: Queen's reads as Queen is; the definition is the queen, consort of William IV

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means placed beneath, so the adviser comes after
dodgy means suspect or unsound, so the letters of deal are jumbled

parts.note: an aide is an assistant, one example of an adviser

explanation.surface: A royal counsellor seems to be backing a shady deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen's adviser' reads as a royal counsellor, but the queen is the definition and ''s' is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The German-born wife of William IV was Britain's queen consort; the Australian city is named after her.

clue.text: European attorney clinches victory for girl

indicators.note: clinches means holds tight, so the attorney's abbreviation wraps around victory

parts.note: DA, district attorney
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A European lawyer secures a win on behalf of a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so a girl in the crossword's loose sense of any woman's name.

clue.text: Opportunity to take cash prize on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen, so the phrase is said aloud

parts.note: to take a cash prize is to win dough, dough being slang for money

explanation.surface: A radio quiz offers a chance to scoop the cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A window is a limited period in which something can be done, as in a window of opportunity.

clue.text: Degenerate English leader of Fascist party

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of the word fascist

parts.note: a fete is a celebration or outdoor party

explanation.surface: A degenerate English fascist leader heads a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Weak, decadent and lacking vigour, the adjectival sense of having degenerated.

clue.text: Legal backing rascal hinted at

indicators.note: backing means coming behind, so legal is placed after the rascal

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child, a rascal
licit means legal, permitted

explanation.surface: Legal support for a scoundrel was only hinted at.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implied but never stated outright is suggested, an adjective sense matching hinted at.

clue.text: Dog died in seaside town

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the abbreviation for died goes within the town

parts.note: Poole is a seaside town on the Dorset coast of southern England

explanation.surface: A dog passed away in a coastal resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A curly-coated breed, one example of a dog.

clue.text: Difficult to follow part of film about fish

indicators.note: to follow means coming after, so difficult is placed last
about means turned round, so the extract's word is read backwards

parts.note: a clip is a short extract of a film
hard means difficult

explanation.surface: Part of a nature film about fish is hard to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but reverses CLIP to PILC.
explanation.definitionFit: A small oily sea fish of the herring family, the adult sardine.

clue.text: Stuff to study

definitions.meaning: to stuff is to pack something tightly
to study hard just before an exam, swotting

explanation.surface: Things one is meant to read up on.
explanation.definitionFit: Packing tightly and last-minute swotting share one verb, the second a figurative packing of facts.

clue.text: Love new range of products available via internet

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
a line is a range of goods a company sells

explanation.surface: A company's beloved new product range is on sale on the web.
explanation.definitionFit: Connected to or obtainable over the web, the adjectival sense matching available via internet.

clue.text: Lascivious expression the French hear regularly

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word hear

explanation.surface: The French are said often to wear a lustful look.
explanation.definitionFit: A lustful or sly sidelong look is a facial expression of that sort.

clue.text: Hawaiians, for example, all dress in lewd pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters of all dress in lewd are a mess to be rearranged

explanation.surface: People from Hawaii all wear shorts in risque underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' reads as trousers or underwear, but in British slang it means rubbish, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawaiians live on islands in the Pacific, so they are an example of the class.
